Stage 15 — the assistant edits designs, calibrates and traces takeoff, approves for a named reviewer, imports price books, exports files and renders a real-life view

9 September 2026 · Development browser (Vite dev server 127.0.0.1:8091 with the user-authorized Gemini key) · desktop 1280x800, tablet 1024x768 for the render · isolated agent-browser profile · real providers gemini-3.8-flash (assistant) and gemini-2.5-flash-image (render) · no build, installation or native run

What changed

Eight new assistant tools close the gap between what the user asks and what the Live assistant can do: editing, moving and removing design entities by ID; two-point calibration, length tracing and review decisions on imported source pages, every one stamped as arriving through the assistant for a named human; CSV price-book import bound to the library revision; DXF/IFC/PDF/register exports with hash receipts; and an AI real-life visualisation of the captured 3D view, shown on the Render pane with provenance. Twenty workflow agents mapped, built and adversarially verified the modules; six verdicts refuted and every major finding was fixed before wiring. Five real-provider journeys on the user's own dev server passed every assertion, including the sentence Daniel had typed into the QA window earlier: 'generate a real life view of this plan'.
